sanskrit: sucitraś citradharmā ca pitāputrau mahārathau pracarantau mahāvīryau droṇena nihatau raṇe
english: Sucitra and Citradharman, father and son, both mighty chariot-warriors of great valor, while they ranged across the field were slain in battle by Droṇa.

sanskrit: vārdhakṣemir mahārāja kṛtvā kadanam āhave bāhlikena mahārāja kauraveṇa nipātitaḥ
english: Vārdhakṣemi, O great king, after wreaking havoc in the fray, was struck down, O great king, by the Kaurava Bāhlika.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketur mahārāja cedīnāṃ pravaro rathaḥ kṛtvā nasukaraṃ karma gato vaivasvatakṣayam
english: Dhṛṣṭaketu, O great king, foremost chariot-warrior of the Cedis, having done a deed hard to accomplish, went to the abode of Vaivasvata.

sanskrit: tathā satyadhṛtis tāta kṛtvā kadanam āhave pāṇḍavārthe parākrānto gamito yamasādanam
english: So too Satyadhṛti, my son, having wrought slaughter in the fray and shown his prowess for the Pāṇḍavas' cause, was sent to the dwelling of Yama.

sanskrit: putras tu śiśupālasya suketuḥ pṛthivīpate nihatya śātravān saṃkhye droṇena nihato yudhi
english: And the son of Śiśupāla, Suketu, O lord of the earth, having slain his foes in the clash, was himself slain in battle by Droṇa.

sanskrit: tathā satyadhṛtir vīro madirāśvaś ca vīryavān sūryadattaś ca vikrānto nihato droṇasāyakaiḥ
english: Likewise the hero Satyadhṛti, the valiant Madirāśva, and the bold Sūryadatta were laid low by the arrows of Droṇa.

sanskrit: śreṇimāṃś ca mahārāja yudhyamānaḥ parākramī kṛtvā nasukaraṃ karma gato vaivasvatakṣayam
english: And Śreṇimat, O great king, valorous as he fought, having performed a deed hard to do, went to the abode of Vaivasvata.

sanskrit: tathaiva yudhi vikrānto māgadhaḥ paravīrahā bhīṣmeṇa nihato rājan yudhyamānaḥ parākramī
english: In the same way the Māgadha, bold in battle, slayer of enemy heroes, valorous as he fought, was slain, O king, by Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: vasudānaś ca kadanaṃ kurvāṇo 'tīva saṃyuge bhāradvājena vikramya gamito yamasādanam
english: And Vasudāna, wreaking great carnage in the conflict, was sent by the prowess of the son of Bharadvāja to the dwelling of Yama.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ hatā droṇena vikramya yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: These and many other great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas were slain by Droṇa through his valor — this is what you ask of me.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca hatapravīre sainye 'smin māmake vadatāṃ vara ahatāñ śaṃsa me sūta ye 'tra jīvanti ke cana
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Now that the foremost heroes of this my army are slain, O best of speakers, tell me, O Sūta, of those unslain — whoever among them still lives.

sanskrit: eteṣu nihateṣv adya ye tvayā parikīrtitāḥ ahatān manyase yāṃs tvaṃ te 'pi svargajito matāḥ
english: Now that those you have named are slain, even those whom you reckon unslain — they too, I deem, are as good as won over by heaven.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yasmin mahāstrāṇi samarpitāni; citrāṇi śubhrāṇi caturvidhāni divyāni rājan nihitāni caiva; droṇena vīradvijasattamena
english: Saṃjaya said: He in whom the great weapons were vested — wondrous, gleaming, of four kinds, and divine, O king — bestowed upon him by Droṇa, best of heroic brahmins;

sanskrit: mahārathaḥ kṛtimān kṣiprahasto; dṛḍhāyudho dṛḍhamuṣṭir dṛḍheṣuḥ sa vīryavān droṇaputras tarasvī; vyavasthito yoddhukāmas tvadarthe
english: that great chariot-warrior, skilled and swift of hand, firm in his weapons, firm in grip, firm in his arrows — the valiant, impetuous son of Droṇa stands ready, eager to fight for your sake.

sanskrit: ānartavāsī hṛdikātmajo 'sau; mahārathaḥ sātvatānāṃ variṣṭhaḥ svayaṃ bhojaḥ kṛtavarmā kṛtāstro; vyavasthito yoddhukāmas tvadarthe
english: That dweller of Ānarta, the son of Hṛdika, a great chariot-warrior, foremost among the Sātvatas — Kṛtavarman the Bhoja himself, master of weapons — stands ready, eager to fight for your sake.

sanskrit: śāradvato gautamaś cāpi rājan; mahābalo bahucitrāstrayodhī dhanuś citraṃ sumahad bhārasāhaṃ; vyavasthito yotsyamānaḥ pragṛhya
english: The son of Śaradvat, the Gautama too, O king, mighty in strength, a fighter with many varied weapons, taking up his wondrous bow, great and able to bear the strain, stands ready and willing to fight.

sanskrit: ārtāyaniḥ samare duṣprakampyaḥ; senāgraṇīḥ prathamas tāvakānām svasreyāṃs tān pāṇḍaveyān visṛjya; satyāṃ vācaṃ tāṃ cikīrṣus tarasvī
english: The son of Ṛtāyana, unshakable in battle, leader of the host, first among your men — having spared those his nephews, the sons of Pāṇḍu, the impetuous one, wishing to make true his pledged word.

sanskrit: tejovadhaṃ sūtaputrasya saṃkhye; pratiśrutvājātaśatroḥ purastāt durādharṣaḥ śakrasamānavīryaḥ; śalyaḥ sthito yoddhukāmas tvadarthe
english: Having vowed before Ajātaśatru in the clash to quell the splendor of the Sūta's son, the unassailable Śalya, of valor equal to Śakra's, stands ready, eager to fight for your sake.

sanskrit: ājāneyaiḥ saindhavaiḥ pārvatīyair; nadījakāmbojavanāyubāhlikaiḥ gāndhārarājaḥ svabalena yukto; vyavasthito yoddhukāmas tvadarthe
english: With horses of high breed, those of Sindhu and the mountains, and the river-born ones of Kāmboja, Vanāyu, and Bāhlika, the king of Gāndhāra, joined with his own host, stands ready, eager to fight for your sake.

sanskrit: tathā sutas te jvalanārkavarṇaṃ; rathaṃ samāsthāya kurupravīra vyavasthitaḥ kurumitro narendra; vyabhre sūryo bhrājamāno yathā vai
english: And your son too, O foremost of the Kurus, mounting a chariot blazing like fire and sun, Kurumitra stands ready, O lord of men, like the sun shining in a cloudless sky.

sanskrit: duryodhano nāgakulasya madhye; mahāvīryaḥ saha sainyapravīraiḥ rathena jāmbūnadabhūṣaṇena; vyavasthitaḥ samare yoddhukāmaḥ
english: Duryodhana, amid his host of elephants, of mighty valor, together with the foremost warriors of the army, on his chariot adorned with gold, stands ready in the battle, eager to fight.

sanskrit: sa rājamadhye puruṣapravīro; rarāja jāmbūnadacitravarmā padmaprabho vahnir ivālpadhūmo; meghāntare sūrya iva prakāśaḥ
english: That foremost of men, amid the kings, shone forth in his bright golden mail, lotus-hued, like a fire with little smoke, radiant as the sun gleaming between the clouds.

sanskrit: tathā suṣeṇo 'py asicarmapāṇis; tavātmajaḥ satyasenaś ca vīraḥ vyavasthitau citrasenena sārdhaṃ; hṛṣṭātmānau samare yoddhukāmau
english: So too Suṣeṇa, sword and shield in hand, your son, and the hero Satyasena, both stand together with Citrasena, glad of heart, eager to fight in the battle.

sanskrit: hrīniṣedhā bharatā rājaputrāś; citrāyudhaḥ śrutakarmā jayaś ca śalaś ca satyavrataduḥśalau ca; vyavasthitā balino yoddhukāmāḥ
english: The Bharata princes who shun all that is shameful — Citrāyudha, Śrutakarman, and Jaya, and Śala, and Satyavrata and Duḥśalā — stand ready, mighty and eager to fight.

sanskrit: kaitavyānām adhipaḥ śūramānī; raṇe raṇe śatruhā rājaputraḥ patrī hayī nāgarathaprayāyī; vyavasthito yoddhukāmas tvadarthe
english: The lord of the Kaitavyas, proud in his valor, a slayer of foes in battle after battle, that prince, with foot and horse, marching with his elephants and chariots, stands ready, eager to fight for your sake.

sanskrit: vīraḥ śrutāyuś ca śrutāyudhaś ca; citrāṅgadaś citravarmā sa vīraḥ vyavasthitā ye tu sainye narāgryāḥ; prahāriṇo māninaḥ satyasaṃdhāḥ
english: The hero Śrutāyus and Śrutāyudha, Citrāṅgada and that hero Citravarman — those foremost of men in the army stand ready, smiters all, proud and true to their pledges.

sanskrit: karṇātmajaḥ satyaseno mahātmā; vyavasthitaḥ samare yoddhukāmaḥ athāparau karṇasutau varārhau; vyavasthitau laghuhastau narendra balaṃ mahad durbhidam alpadhairyaiḥ; samāśritau yotsyamānau tvadarthe
english: The son of Karṇa, the high-souled Satyasena, stands ready in battle, eager to fight; and two other worthy sons of Karṇa, deft of hand, O lord of men, stand ready, leaning upon a mighty host hard for the faint-hearted to break, willing to fight for your sake.

sanskrit: etaiś ca mukhyair aparaiś ca rājan; yodhapravīrair amitaprabhāvaiḥ vyavasthito nāgakulasya madhye; yathā mahendraḥ kururājo jayāya
english: With these and other chief warriors, foremost in arms, of boundless might, the king of the Kurus stands amid his host of elephants, like great Indra, bent on victory.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ākhyātā jīvamānā ye parebhyo 'nye yathātatham itīdam abhigacchāmi vyaktam arthābhipattitaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: You have told me truly of those who yet live and of the others as well; thus I clearly perceive how things will come to pass, by reckoning the course of events.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ bruvann eva tadā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ hatapravīraṃ vidhvastaṃ kiṃciccheṣaṃ svakaṃ balam śrutvā vyāmoham agamac chokavyākulitendriyaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Even as he spoke thus, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the son of Ambikā, hearing that his own army was shattered, its heroes slain, with but a remnant left, fell into a swoon, his senses overwhelmed by grief.

sanskrit: muhyamāno 'bravīc cāpi muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭha saṃjaya vyākulaṃ me manas tāta śrutvā sumahad apriyam naṣṭacittas tataḥ so 'tha babhūva jagatīpatiḥ
english: Swooning, he said: Hold a moment, Saṃjaya; my mind is distraught, my son, hearing of so great a sorrow. And then the lord of the earth lost his senses.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca śrutvā karṇaṃ hataṃ yuddhe putrāṃś caivāpalāyinaḥ narendraḥ kiṃ cid āśvasto dvijaśreṣṭha kim abravīt
english: Janamejaya said: Hearing that Karṇa was slain in the battle and that his sons did not flee, what did the king, somewhat recovered, then say, O best of the twice-born?

sanskrit: prāptavān paramaṃ duḥkhaṃ putravyasanajaṃ mahat tasmin yad uktavān kāle tan mamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ
english: He who had won the utmost grief, the great sorrow born of his sons' ruin — what he said at that hour, tell me that, for I ask of you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvā karṇasya nidhanam aśraddheyam ivādbhutam bhūtasaṃmohanaṃ bhīmaṃ meroḥ paryasanaṃ yathā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing of Karṇa's death — incredible, marvelous, bewildering to all beings, and terrible as the overturning of Meru;

sanskrit: cittamoham ivāyuktaṃ bhārgavasya mahāmateḥ parājayam ivendrasya dviṣadbhyo bhīmakarmaṇaḥ
english: like an unaccountable bewilderment of mind in the wise descendant of Bhṛgu, like a defeat of Indra of fearsome deeds at the hands of his foes;

sanskrit: divaḥ prapatanaṃ bhānor urvyām iva mahādyuteḥ saṃśoṣaṇam ivācintyaṃ samudrasyākṣayāmbhasaḥ
english: like the fall of the radiant sun from heaven to the earth, like the unthinkable drying up of the ocean of inexhaustible waters;

sanskrit: mahīviyaddigīśānāṃ sarvanāśam ivādbhutam karmaṇor iva vaiphalyam ubhayoḥ puṇyapāpayoḥ
english: like the marvelous total destruction of earth, sky, and the guardians of the quarters, like the fruitlessness of both deeds, the meritorious and the sinful alike.

sanskrit: saṃcintya nipuṇaṃ buddhyā dhṛtarāṣṭro janeśvaraḥ nedam astīti saṃcintya karṇasya nidhanaṃ prati
english: Pondering it shrewdly in his mind, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the people, reflecting upon Karṇa's death, thought: "This cannot be."

sanskrit: prāṇinām etad ātmatvāt syād apīti vināśanam śokāgninā dahyamāno dhamyamāna ivāśayaḥ
english: "Yet, since this is the very nature of living things, such destruction may indeed be" — and his heart was consumed by the fire of grief, as though fanned into flame.

sanskrit: vidhvastātmā śvasan dīno hā hety uktvā suduḥkhitaḥ vilalāpa mahārāja dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ
english: His spirit broken, sighing, wretched, crying "Alas, alas!" in deep anguish, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the son of Ambikā, lamented, O great king.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca saṃjayādhiratho vīraḥ siṃhadviradavikramaḥ vṛṣam apratimaskandho vṛṣabhākṣagatisvanaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Saṃjaya, the heroic son of Adhiratha, of the prowess of a lion and an elephant, the bull among men of matchless shoulders, with the eyes, the gait, and the voice of a bull;

sanskrit: vṛṣabho vṛṣabhasyeva yo yuddhe na nivartate śatror api mahendrasya vajrasaṃhanano yuvā
english: a bull who, like a bull, would not turn back in battle even from great Indra his foe — young, his frame hard as the thunderbolt;

sanskrit: yasya jyātalaśabdena śaravṛṣṭiraveṇa ca rathāśvanaramātaṅgā nāvatiṣṭhanti saṃyuge
english: he at the twang of whose bowstring and palm-guard and the roar of whose shower of arrows, chariots, horses, men, and elephants could not stand their ground in the fray;

sanskrit: yam āśritya mahābāhuṃ dviṣatsaṃghaghnam acyutam duryodhano 'karod vairaṃ pāṇḍuputrair mahābalaiḥ
english: relying upon whom — the mighty-armed, unfaltering destroyer of enemy hosts — Duryodhana waged his feud against the sons of Pāṇḍu of great strength:

sanskrit: sa kathaṃ rathināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ karṇaḥ pārthena saṃyuge nihataḥ puruṣavyāghraḥ prasahyāsahyavikramaḥ
english: how was that best of chariot-warriors, Karṇa, the tiger among men of irresistible prowess, slain by force in battle by Pārtha?

sanskrit: yo nāmanyata vai nityam acyutaṃ na dhanaṃjayam na vṛṣṇīn api tān anyān svabāhubalam āśritaḥ
english: He who, ever relying on the might of his own arm, esteemed neither the unfaltering Kṛṣṇa nor Dhanaṃjaya, nor those other Vṛṣṇis;

sanskrit: śārṅgagāṇḍīvadhanvānau sahitāv aparājitau ahaṃ divyād rathād ekaḥ pātayiṣyāmi saṃyuge
english: who said, "The wielders of the Śārṅga and the Gāṇḍīva, united and unvanquished — I alone shall bring them down from their divine chariot in battle";

sanskrit: iti yaḥ satataṃ mandam avocal lobhamohitam duryodhanam apādīnaṃ rājyakāmukam āturam
english: thus spoke he ever to that dullard, Duryodhana, deluded by greed, base, craving the kingdom, and distressed.

sanskrit: yaś cājaiṣīd atibalān amitrān api durjayān gāndhārān madrakān matsyāṃs trigartāṃs taṅgaṇāñ śakān
english: He who conquered foes most mighty and hard to subdue — the Gāndhāras, the Madrakas, the Matsyas, the Trigartas, the Taṅgaṇas, the Śakas;

sanskrit: pāñcālāṃś ca videhāṃś ca kuṇindān kāśikosalān suhmān aṅgāṃś ca puṇḍrāṃś ca niṣādān vaṅgakīcakān
english: the Pāñcālas and the Videhas, the Kuṇindas, the Kāśis and Kosalas, the Suhmas and the Aṅgas, the Puṇḍras, the Niṣādas, the Vaṅgas, and the Kīcakas;

sanskrit: vatsān kaliṅgāṃs taralān aśmakān ṛṣikāṃs tathā yo jitvā samare vīraś cakre balibhṛtaḥ purā
english: the Vatsas, the Kaliṅgas, the Taralas, the Aśmakas, and the Ṛṣikas as well — that hero, having conquered them in battle, made them tribute-bearers of old.

sanskrit: uccaiḥśravā varo 'śvānāṃ rājñāṃ vaiśravaṇo varaḥ varo mahendro devānāṃ karṇaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ
english: As Uccaiḥśravas is the best of horses, as Vaiśravaṇa is the best of kings, as great Indra is the best of the gods, so Karṇa was the best of smiters.

sanskrit: yaṃ labdhvā māgadho rājā sāntvamānārthagauravaiḥ arautsīt pārthivaṃ kṣatram ṛte kauravayādavān
english: He whom the king of Magadha, having won, by conciliation, honor, gifts, and esteem, hemmed in all the warrior princes of the earth, save the Kauravas and the Yādavas.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā nihataṃ karṇaṃ dvairathe savyasācinā śokārṇave nimagno 'ham aplavaḥ sāgare yathā
english: Hearing that Karṇa was slain in single combat by Savyasācin, I am plunged in an ocean of grief, like one without a raft upon the sea.

sanskrit: īdṛśair yady ahaṃ duḥkhair na vinaśyāmi saṃjaya vajrād dṛḍhataraṃ manye hṛdayaṃ mama durbhidam
english: If I am not destroyed by such sorrows, Saṃjaya, I deem my heart harder than the thunderbolt and impossible to break.

sanskrit: jñātisaṃbandhimitrāṇām imaṃ śrutvā parājayam ko mad anyaḥ pumāṃl loke na jahyāt sūta jīvitam
english: Hearing of this defeat of kinsmen, relations, and friends, what other man in the world but me, O Sūta, would not give up his life?

sanskrit: viṣam agniṃ prapātaṃ vā parvatāgrād ahaṃ vṛṇe na hi śakṣyāmi duḥkhāni soḍhuṃ kaṣṭāni saṃjaya
english: I would choose poison, or fire, or a plunge from a mountain's peak; for I shall not be able to bear these grievous sorrows, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śriyā kulena yaśasā tapasā ca śrutena ca tvām adya santo manyante yayātim iva nāhuṣam
english: Saṃjaya said: For your splendor, your lineage, your fame, your austerity, and your learning, the good this day reckon you the equal of Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa.

sanskrit: śrute maharṣipratimaḥ kṛtakṛtyo 'si pārthiva paryavasthāpayātmānaṃ mā viṣāde manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: In learning you are the peer of a great sage; you have fulfilled your purpose, O king. Compose yourself; do not set your mind upon despair.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca daivam eva paraṃ manye dhik pauruṣam anarthakam yatra rāmapratīkāśaḥ karṇo 'hanyata saṃyuge
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: I deem fate supreme; a curse upon manly effort, which is in vain — for there Karṇa, the equal of Rāma, was slain in battle.

sanskrit: hatvā yudhiṣṭhirānīkaṃ pāñcālānāṃ rathavrajān pratāpya śaravarṣeṇa diśaḥ sarvā mahārathaḥ
english: That great chariot-warrior, having slain Yudhiṣṭhira's host and the chariot-squadrons of the Pāñcālas, scorching all the quarters with his rain of arrows —

sanskrit: mohayitvā raṇe pārthān vajrahasta ivāsurān sa kathaṃ nihataḥ śete vātarugṇa iva drumaḥ
english: having bewildered the Pārthas in battle as the thunderbolt-handed one bewilders the Asuras — how is it that he, slain, lies low like a tree shattered by the wind?

sanskrit: śokasyāntaṃ na paśyāmi samudrasyeva viplukāḥ cintā me vardhate tīvrā mumūrṣā cāpi jāyate
english: I see no end to my grief, as a drowning man sees none to the ocean. My sharp anguish grows, and a longing to die is born in me.

sanskrit: karṇasya nidhanaṃ śrutvā vijayaṃ phalgunasya ca aśraddheyam ahaṃ manye vadhaṃ karṇasya saṃjaya
english: Hearing of Karṇa's death and of Phalguna's victory, I hold the slaying of Karṇa beyond belief, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: vajrasāramayaṃ nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ mama yac chrutvā puruṣavyāghraṃ hataṃ karṇaṃ na dīryate
english: Surely my heart is made of the essence of adamant, and most firm, since, hearing that Karṇa, the tiger among men, is slain, it does not burst asunder.

sanskrit: āyur nūnaṃ sudīrghaṃ me vihitaṃ daivataiḥ purā yatra karṇaṃ hataṃ śrutvā jīvāmīha suduḥkhitaḥ
english: Surely a very long life was ordained for me by the gods of old, since, hearing that Karṇa is slain, I yet live on here in deep sorrow.

sanskrit: dhig jīvitam idaṃ me 'dya suhṛd dhīnasya saṃjaya adya cāhaṃ daśām etāṃ gataḥ saṃjaya garhitām kṛpaṇaṃ vartayiṣyāmi śocyaḥ sarvasya mandadhīḥ
english: A curse upon this life of mine today, bereft of friends, Saṃjaya. This day, Saṃjaya, fallen into this contemptible state, I shall pass my days in misery, pitiable to all, dull of wit.

sanskrit: aham eva purā bhūtvā sarvalokasya satkṛtaḥ paribhūtaḥ kathaṃ sūta punaḥ śakṣyāmi jīvitum duḥkhāt suduḥkhaṃ vyasanaṃ prāptavān asmi saṃjaya
english: I who once was honored by all the world — how, O Sūta, despised, shall I be able to live on again? From sorrow to deeper sorrow I have come, into calamity, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: tasmād bhīṣmavadhe caiva droṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ nātra śeṣaṃ prapaśyāmi sūtaputre hate yudhi
english: Therefore, after the slaying of Bhīṣma and of the high-souled Droṇa, now that the Sūta's son too is slain in battle, I see no remnant left.

sanskrit: sa hi pāraṃ mahān āsīt putrāṇāṃ mama saṃjaya yuddhe vinihataḥ śūro visṛjan sāyakān bahūn
english: For he was the great further shore for my sons, Saṃjaya — that hero, slain in battle while loosing many arrows.

sanskrit: ko hi me jīvitenārthas tam ṛte puruṣarṣabham rathād atiratho nūnam apatat sāyakārditaḥ
english: What use is life to me without that bull among men? That surpassing chariot-warrior must have fallen from his car, tormented by arrows,

sanskrit: parvatasyeva śikharaṃ vajrapātavidāritam śayīta pṛthivīṃ nūnaṃ śobhayan rudhirokṣitaḥ mātaṅga iva mattena mātaṅgena nipātitaḥ
english: like a mountain's peak riven by the fall of the thunderbolt; surely he lies upon the earth, adorning it, drenched in blood, like an elephant struck down by a rutting elephant.

sanskrit: yad balaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ yato bhayam so 'rjunena hataḥ karṇaḥ pratimānaṃ dhanuṣmatām
english: He who was the strength of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and from whom came the Pāṇḍavas' fear — that Karṇa, the standard by which bowmen are measured, was slain by Arjuna.

sanskrit: sa hi vīro maheṣvāsaḥ putrāṇām abhayaṃkaraḥ śete vinihato vīraḥ śakreṇeva yathā balaḥ
english: For that hero, the great archer, who gave my sons their freedom from fear — that hero now lies slain, as Bala was slain by Śakra.

sanskrit: paṅgor ivādhvagamanaṃ daridrasyeva kāmitam duryodhanasya cākūtaṃ tṛṣitasyeva piplukāḥ
english: Duryodhana's design has proved like the journeying of a cripple, like the desire of a pauper, like the water-droplets craved by one athirst.

sanskrit: anyathā cintitaṃ kāryam anyathā tat tu jāyate aho nu balavad daivaṃ kālaś ca duratikramaḥ
english: The deed is purposed one way, yet it comes to pass in another. Ah, how mighty is fate, and how impossible to overstep is time!

sanskrit: palāyamānaḥ kṛpaṇaṃ dīnātmā dīnapauruṣaḥ kaccin na nihataḥ sūta putro duḥśāsano mama
english: Fleeing piteously, his spirit broken, his manhood failing — has my son Duḥśāsana not been slain, O Sūta?

sanskrit: kaccin na nīcācaritaṃ kṛtavāṃs tāta saṃyuge kaccin na nihataḥ śūro yathā na kṣatriyā hatāḥ
english: Did he not act basely in the fray, my son? Was that hero not slain — slain not as warriors are slain in honor?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasya vacanaṃ mā yuddham iti sarvadā duryodhano nābhyagṛhṇān mūḍhaḥ pathyam ivauṣadham
english: Yudhiṣṭhira's word, ever "Let there be no war" — that the deluded Duryodhana would not accept, as a fool will not take wholesome medicine.

sanskrit: śaratalpe śayānena bhīṣmeṇa sumahātmanā pānīyaṃ yācitaḥ pārthaḥ so 'vidhyan medinītalam
english: When Bhīṣma, that most high-souled one, lying upon his bed of arrows, asked for water, Pārtha pierced the surface of the earth.
